summary: Final release certification of the MOD Operations fixes made after iter323. The review request I received was truncated ('MOD Operations + Co…'), so the scope was taken from the latest commit diff and PRD: bfpo.py deactivation decisions and holds, bfpo_coverage handling of existing ids, follow-up customer email states, the Schedule B boot lock, StaffEngineers dangling chips and the DeactivateEngineerModal override. A broad MOD and Contracts regression was also run. Backend: regression (iter323 integrity, chase x2, bootstrap race) passes 40/40. Broad regression (bfpo invite/portal, iter322 wizard/delete, system access iter321, Contract Management workspace) passes 88/88, 4 skipped, after 2 stale CM test expectations were updated. The new tests/test_release_cert_iter324.py passes 9/12. Results: reassigning outside coverage during deactivation without override_reason returns 422 code outside_coverage and applies nothing; with a reason it returns 200 and the override is in the timeline and in extra.coverage_override. Keep becomes a management hold (unassigned, management_hold, held_from_engineer_id). The hold survives reactivation and allocate clears it. The iter323 HIGH invite reactivation fix is verified: deactivation deletes the invite and accept returns 403. A staff PATCH with a dangling site id returns 200, removal works and a new unknown id returns 422. The follow-up run creates an awaiting_approval email with a unique (group, chase, revision) index; a re-run creates no duplicate and the schedule status is task_created. Release returns 409 while sending is off, a rep gets 403, a bad action 422 and an unknown follow-up 404. Cancel returns 200, a second cancel 409. dispatch_ready with send_email mocked sends exactly once under 2 concurrent dispatchers and records message_id. UI (modsales.manager at /bfpo): the follow-up card shows the email status chip, the reason, Release email (an error toast while off) and Don't send (status becomes cancelled, buttons hide). The engineer edit modal shows the 'Unknown reference ✕' chip; a name-only save works and clicking the chip removes the reference. The deactivate modal shows the override input after the outside-coverage error and saves with the reason. NEW bugs: 1 HIGH (engineers can take over held jobs or jobs allocated to someone else), 1 MEDIUM (Master Admin PATCH still blocked by dangling ids), 1 MEDIUM UI (chase chips still say 'scheduled' after a chase is raised).

critical.issue: Any engineer whose territory or sites cover a job can accept it, even when it is (a) held for management review (management_hold true, assigned null) or (b) already allocated to another engineer. Accept overwrites assigned_engineer_id with no checks and leaves management_hold:true on the case. In the repro, the peer gets 200 and becomes the assignee in both cases. Held jobs also appear in in-coverage engineers' GET /bfpo/jobs. Root cause: _get_scoped_case(read=False) only checks territory/site scope, and bfpo_accept does not check the current assignee or the hold. This defeats the new 'Hold for management review' decision and lets an engineer take a job that staff allocated to someone else. Fix: in bfpo_accept, refuse with 409 when management_hold is true, or when assigned_engineer_id is set and is not the caller (staff/lead may override). Exclude management_hold cases from the engineer queue query.

minor.issue: Parity gap with the iter323 fix. master_admin_mod_estate.py:2204 calls validate_allocation without existing_t/existing_s, so a Master Admin edit that resends an engineer's existing dangling id still returns 422 'Coverage not saved — unknown site X'. MOD Ops PATCH (bfpo.py:1307) passes them. Fix: pass eng.get('bfpo_territory_ids') and eng.get('bfpo_site_ids') as the 3rd and 4th args. The same applies at line 1872 for the bulk path, if relevant.
There is no organization_id scoping on the follow-up lookup; any MOD sales manager can act on a follow-up by id. Low risk with a single operator org.
Only the first outside-coverage job is reported per 422. With several such jobs the user has to submit repeatedly to reveal each override input.
_migrate_legacy only runs in run_chases, so legacy follow-ups have no email_status (the UI shows '—') until the next cron or manual run. The preview DB is already migrated.

ui_bugs.issue: chase_schedule status is now 'task_created' (was 'done'), but the chip still only maps 'done' to 'chased'. A raised chase shows '2 weeks · 01/01/2026 · scheduled' in pending style. Verified in the UI. Map task_created (and done, for legacy) to the 'chased' label and style.

issues: 'Release email' is shown and clickable while customer emails are switched off or the wording is unapproved, but it always fails with a 409 error toast. Hide or disable it, with a tooltip, unless live sending is on and the wording is approved.
Cancel and 'Deactivate engineer' are still both filled blue (carried over from iter323). Make Deactivate destructive and Cancel secondary.
The reassign dropdown does not mark out-of-coverage engineers up front; the override input appears only after a failed submit.
About 25 'Async Site 0 (MOD establishment)' mod_site orgs (leftover test data from other suites) flood the picker and /bfpo/sites. There is still no search or grouping.

action_items: HIGH: bfpo_accept must refuse (409) when the case has management_hold or is assigned to a different engineer. Exclude management_hold cases from the engineer /bfpo/jobs queue.
MEDIUM: master_admin_mod_estate.py:2204 — pass the engineer's existing bfpo_territory_ids/bfpo_site_ids into validate_allocation (parity with bfpo.py:1307)
MEDIUM: ModQuoteGroup.js chase chips — treat 'task_created' as chased
UX: hide or disable 'Release email' while live sending is off or the wording is unapproved. Style Deactivate as destructive.
Data hygiene: remove the ~25 'Async Site 0' test mod_site orgs that pollute the coverage pickers (find the suite that creates them)
critical_code_review_comments: mod_quote_chase state machine is solid: separate email_status, a unique index for idempotency, an atomic find_one_and_update claim with a lease, interrupted sends going to failed for human review, and auto-retry capped at MAX_ATTEMPTS.

If the unique index create_index ever fails on legacy duplicate (group, chase, null revision) docs, run_chases raises on every run. No duplicates exist in preview, but consider a try/except or a dedupe migration before production.
The release endpoint checks the group status against a literal tuple while dispatch uses ACTIVE. Use ACTIVE in both places to avoid drift.

Schedule B _take_lock: a lock older than 10 minutes is deleted by any replica. If a bootstrap ever runs longer than that, two replicas could run concurrently. This is acceptable for the current workload.
routes/bfpo.py (~1640 lines) and master_admin_mod_estate.py (~2300 lines) remain well over the 700-line guideline.
